specAmbiguitiesResolved: Paid contact authority: M09 does not exist, so a paid execute names {approvalId, executionAuthorityId}. M07 verifies the M02 PLAN_ACTION approval is executable and exactly scoped (incident, site, asset/evidence/policy revisions, action digest, plan hash, pinned account revision, paid, currency, max >= request cap); the execution-authority id is passed opaque to the broker port, which must verify it (M09).

Paid action digest: computeActionDigest with action {kind PAID_CONTACT, subjectId = service provider id, quantity 1}, merchantId and amount = the request's paid cap, purpose = contact purpose; plan hash = canonicalDigest('provider-contact-plan', 1, {actionDigest, requestDigest}) (a single-action plan until M08). Unpaid requests carry no action digest; their identity is the request digest.

Broker hand-off: M07 calls createIntent then execute exactly once (serialized per request with a session advisory lock); it never calls reconcile. Results returned by execute and later outbox events go through the same mirror (dedupe by event id, STALE by aggregate version, quarantine on unknown intent/binding/origin).
checkDecisionExecutable (M06) is not called: quote/availability contacts precede compatibility decisions and a quote never approves compatibility; M08/M09 gate part purchases with it.

Unpaid execute only queues a PREPARED attempt plus a provider.contact_dispatch job; the worker commits SEND_STARTED before egress. Supersession between queue and dispatch makes the queued attempt definite no-effect and invalidates the request.

Webhooks are authoritative only for provider acknowledgement ('received' -> ACCEPTED); other statuses schedule lookup. A superseded revision's verifier is accepted for 24 h, and only for attempts pinned to that revision. Broker-owned bindings are refused.

Transcript processing consent: an excerpt is stored and usable only with the latest PROCESSING consent GRANTED (fail closed even when the request says NOT_REQUIRED). Promotion to M05 is the minimum excerpt as a consented TRANSCRIPT document. M05's tool search never returns transcript spans, so the excerpt reaches a model only via the packet's selection.
Retention: retain_until = min(tenant RETENTION communicationDays, class default 30/365 days).

Contact destinations: the request names a contactPointId; usable when the latest admin review is VERIFIED, or unreviewed, DISCOVERED and from the request's pinned account revision. Contact-point review uses provider.vendor_link (admin).
Site-scope denials on M07 resources look like absence (FORBIDDEN RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE); readers lacking a specific action get the ordinary audited FORBIDDEN.
Notification routing is code-versioned (notification-routing.v1) rather than tenant-configurable; channel is LOCAL_INBOX only.
Consent withdrawal by the provider (provider-API sourced) may be recorded by the engine (provider.engine); humans record consent as operators (provider.contact).
securityReview: Coordinator findings fixed test-first (d7637ae red, d560728 green): (1) DNS rebinding TOCTOU -> connect-time guardedLookup on node:https; (2) contact-point destination hijack -> provenance, intake state, admin review, required contactPointId, DB guard; (3) excerpt/promotion checks before authorization -> scope authorized first, denial identical to absence; (4) client-supplied transcript provenance -> server-derived, mismatch refused.

Coordinator finding 5 fixed test-first (07d3fdf red, c20ca15 green): consent withdrawal withdrew promoted documents after the consent transaction with the caller's evidence permission and LIMIT 100 -> withdrawn in the same transaction as an unbounded system action; promotion serialized with withdrawal by a per-request advisory lock (101 promoted documents plus racing promotions leave zero active documents).

Coordinator finding 6 fixed test-first (8987f62 red, ending commit green): promotion held a session advisory lock on one pooled client while taking more pooled connections (pool deadlock; a failed unlock returned a locked client) -> one-transaction promotion with pg_advisory_xact_lock and ingestDocumentInTx; the paid hand-off does all work on its lock connection with a bounded try-lock and destroys the client on unlock failure. Six promotions racing a withdrawal and five paid hand-offs complete on a 2-connection pool with no advisory lock left.

Self-review findings fixed in the same commits: provider-controlled raw status/reference strings could violate column CHECKs and strand a SEND_STARTED marker -> sanitized tokens; withdrawn processing consent left promoted excerpt evidence in future packets -> promoted M05 documents withdrawn.

Pinned by regression tests: webhook signature/tamper/stale/replay/broker-owned/oversize/unknown binding, tenant-routed webhook targets, broker-event quarantine, pagination bounds (max pages, cursor cycle, max results), provider text normalization, SSRF URL/IP/redirect/size/policy-binding cases.
unresolvedRisks: No real provider, StablePhone/StableEmail/StableEnrich, relay, telephony or Kite path has run; every adapter result is SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE, LOCAL_FAKE or CONTRACT_FAKE.
The execution-authority id of a paid contact is not verified by M07 (no authority table until M09); M09's broker must reload and bind it to the approval.
Approval revocation between M07's check and the broker call is a TOCTOU the broker must close (it rechecks before reserve).

Rate limits and the per-revision token bucket are in-process; multi-instance deployments need a shared budget. Invalid webhook deliveries are recorded (M02 design) and are an unauthenticated write amplification without an edge rate limit.
Sweeps (sweepContactAttempts, runContactDispatch, runWebhookApply, dispatchNotifications) must be scheduled by the deployed process (M14); nothing runs them on a timer.
A crash between search persistence phases leaves a search PENDING (no sweep marks it); searches have no effect, so this is cosmetic.
Redaction is pattern-based (emails, phones, cards, IBAN, secrets, URLs); names are not detected and are excluded only by the minimum-excerpt line filter.
Notification recipients/roles and routing table are code-defined; spend-exception routing covers paid contact intents only (plan-action intents are M09/M10's trigger).

M09 broker-port contract to satisfy (CommercialIntentBrokerPort, @uptimebuyer/kite-contracts): createIntent must be idempotent on (tenant, actionDigest, executionAuthorityId) for M07's request {subject {type PROVIDER_CONTACT_REQUEST, id pcr_}, semanticOperation PAID_CONTACT, providerAccountRevisionId = the request's pinned revision, actionDigest, planHash, approvalId, executionAuthorityId, expectedMax = request cap, idempotencyKey pcr.<request>.<authority>} and return an intent whose tenant/subject/actionDigest/authority/revision echo the request (M07 rejects a mismatch); execute is called once per new intent and must never re-send a started intent; M07 never calls reconcile. M09 must verify the execution authority belongs to the approval, recheck the approval before reserve, and publish commercial_intent.state_changed.v1 to the outbox with monotonically increasing aggregate versions, resultOrigin KITE_BROKER, attempt views on every SEND_STARTED/ACKNOWLEDGED/UNKNOWN change, nextReconcileAt on UNKNOWN (null only with adapterCapability UNSUPPORTED); M07's consumer is handleBrokerResultEvent / consumer name provider-broker-result.v1.

M09/M11 notification triggers: enqueueNotificationTrigger(client, ctx, {triggerKind SPEND_EXCEPTION|APPROVAL_REQUIRED|RECOVERY|EVIDENCE_GAP|..., sourceEventId, sourceEventType, logicalKey, incidentId, reasonCode, titleCode?, recipientUserIds?, deepLink?, context?}) inside the emitting transaction (engine/worker context), or emit outbox events consumed by handleNotificationEvent (consumer provider-notifications.v1). dispatchNotifications(pool, port) and LocalNotificationInbox are the delivery side; M12 T-051 owns the end-to-end check.

M14 wiring: schedule runContactDispatch, sweepContactAttempts, runWebhookApply, dispatchNotifications and the two consumers; configure HttpsProviderTransport (endpoint policy must hash to the revision's endpoint_policy_digest) and unpaid credentials via a CredentialResolver; expose ingestProviderWebhook at /v1/provider-webhooks/{binding}.
